title: Science of setbacks: How failure can improve career prospects ｜ 挫折的科学：失败如何改善职业前景

sents.en: How do early career setbacks affect our long-term success?
sents.cn: 早期职业挫折会如何影响我们的长期成功？

sents.en: Failures can help us learn and overcome our fears. But disasters can still wound us. They can screw us up and set us back.
sents.cn: 失败能帮助我们学习并克服恐惧，但灾难仍可能伤害我们，把我们搞得一团糟、让我们倒退。

sents.en: Wouldn't it be nice if there was genuine, scientifically documented truth to the expression "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger"?
sents.cn: 如果"那些杀不死你的，会让你更强大"这句话真有经科学证实的依据，那该多好？

sents.en: One way social scientists have probed the effects of career setbacks is to look at scientists of very similar qualifications.
sents.cn: 社会科学家探究职业挫折影响的一种方式，是考察资质极为相似的科学家。这些科学家大多出于偶然原因，要么刚好错过一笔研究资助，要么刚好拿到。

sents.en: These scientists, for reasons that are mostly arbitrary, either just missed getting a research grant or just barely made it. In social sciences, this is known as examining "near misses" and "narrow wins" in areas where merit is subjective.
sents.cn: 在社会科学中，这被称为考察"擦肩而过"（nearmisses）与"险胜"（narrowwins）那些功绩带有主观性的领域。

sents.en: That allows researchers to measure only the effects of being chosen or not.
sents.cn: 这能让研究者只衡量"被选中与否"的影响。

sents.en: Studies in this area have found conflicting results.
sents.cn: 该领域的研究得出了相互矛盾的结果。

sents.en: In the competitive game of biomedical science, research has been done on scientists who narrowly lost or won grant money. It suggests that narrow winners become even bigger winners down the line. In other words, the rich get richer.
sents.cn: 在竞争激烈的生物医学科学中，有人对险胜或惜败于资助金的科学家做了研究，结果表明险胜者日后会变得更加成功——换句话说，富者愈富。

sents.en: A 2018 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, for example, followed researchers in the Netherlands.
sents.cn: 例如，2018年发表于《美国国家科学院院刊》的一项研究，追踪了荷兰的研究人员。

sents.en: Researchers concluded that those who just barely qualified for a grant were able to get twice as much money within the next eight years as those who just missed out.
sents.cn: 研究者得出结论：那些刚好够格获得资助的人，在接下来八年里拿到的钱，是那些刚好落选者的两倍；

sents.en: And the narrow winners were 50 percent more likely to be given a professorship.
sents.cn: 而且险胜者获得教授职位的可能性高出50%。

sents.en: Others in the US have found similar effects with National Institutes of Health early-career fellowships launching narrow winners far ahead of close losers.
sents.cn: 美国其他研究者也发现类似效应：美国国立卫生研究院的早期职业奖学金，让险胜者远远领先于惜败者。

sents.en: The phenomenon is often referred to as the Matthew effect, inspired by the Bible's wisdom that to those who have, more will be given.
sents.cn: 这种现象常被称为"马太效应"（Mattheweffect），其灵感来自《圣经》的智慧——"凡有的，还要加给他"。

sents.en: There's a good explanation for the phenomenon in the book The Formula: The Universal Laws of Success by Albert Laszlo Barabasi.
sents.cn: 阿尔伯特∙拉斯洛∙巴拉巴西在《公式：成功的普适法则》一书中，对这一现象给出了很好的解释。

sents.en: According to Barabasi, it's easier and less risky for those in positions of power to choose to hand awards and funding to those who've already been so recognized.
sents.cn: 巴拉巴西认为，掌权者把奖项和资金交给那些已被认可的人，是更容易、风险也更低的选择。

sents.en: This is bad news for the losers.
sents.cn: 这对落选者是个坏消息。

sents.en: Small early career setbacks seem to have a disproportionate effect down the line. What didn't kill them made them weaker.
sents.cn: 早期职业生涯中的小挫折，似乎会在日后产生不成比例的影响——没杀死他们的，反而让他们更弱。

sents.en: But other studies using the same technique have shown there's sometimes no penalty to a near miss.
sents.cn: 但使用同一技术的其他研究发现，有时"擦肩而过"并无惩罚。

sents.en: Students who just miss getting into top high schools or universities do just as well later in life as those who just manage to get accepted.
sents.cn: 那些刚好没考入顶尖高中或大学的学生，日后的人生表现与那些刚好被录取的人一样好。

sents.en: In this case, what didn't kill them simply didn't matter.
sents.cn: 在这种情况下，没杀死他们的，其实无关紧要。

sents.en: So is there any evidence that setbacks might actually improve our career prospects?
sents.cn: 那么，有没有证据表明挫折实际上能改善我们的职业前景？

sents.en: There is now.
sents.cn: 现在有了。

sents.en: In a study published in Nature Communications, Northwestern University sociologist Dashun Wang tracked more than 1,100 scientists who were on the border between getting a grant and missing out between 1990 and 2005. He followed various measures of performance over the next decade.
sents.cn: 在发表于《自然∙通讯》的一项研究中，西北大学社会学家王大顺（DashunWang）追踪了1990至2005年间1100多名"介于拿到与错过资助之间"的科学家。

sents.en: These included how many papers they authored and how influential those papers were, as measured by the number of subsequent citations. As expected, there was a much higher rate of attrition among scientists who didn't get grants.
sents.cn: 他在随后十年里跟踪了多种表现指标，包括他们发表了多少论文，以及这些论文的影响力（以后续被引次数衡量）。

sents.en: But among those who stayed on, the close losers performed even better than the narrow winners.
sents.cn: 正如预期，未获资助的科学家流失率高得多。但在留下的人当中，惜败者的表现甚至优于险胜者。

sents.en: To make sure this wasn't by chance, Wang conducted additional tests using different performance measures. He examined how many times people were first authors on influential studies, and the like.
sents.cn: 为确保这不是偶然，王进行了额外的检验，使用了不同的表现指标，考察人们在有影响力的研究中作为第一作者的次数等。

sents.en: One straightforward reason close losers might outperform narrow winners is that the two groups have comparable ability.
sents.cn: 惜败者可能胜过险胜者的一个直接原因是：两组能力相当。

sents.en: In Wang's study, he selected the most determined, passionate scientists from the loser group and culled what he deemed the weakest members of the winner group.
sents.cn: 在王的研究中，他从落选组中挑出最坚定、最有热情的科学家，并剔除他认为胜出组中最弱的成员。

sents.en: Yet the persevering losers still came out on top.
sents.cn: 然而，那些坚持不懈的落选者仍位居前列。

sents.en: He thinks that being a close loser might give people a psychological boost, or the proverbial kick in the pants.
sents.cn: 他认为，惜败或许能给人心理上的鼓舞，即俗语所说的"在屁股上踢一脚"。

sents.en: Utrecht University sociologist Arnout van de Rijt was the lead author on the 2018 paper showing the rich get richer.
sents.cn: 乌得勒支大学社会学家阿尔诺∙范德赖特是2018年那篇"富者愈富"论文的第一作者。

sents.en: He said the new finding is apparently reasonable and worth some attention.
sents.cn: 他说，这一新发现显然合理，值得关注。

sents.en: His own work showed that although the narrow winners did get much more money in the near future, the actual performance of the close losers was just as good.
sents.cn: 他自己的研究表明，尽管险胜者近期确实拿到了更多钱，但惜败者的实际表现同样出色。

sents.en: He said the people who should be paying regard to the Wang paper are the funding agents who distribute government grant money.
sents.cn: 他说，应当关注王这篇论文的，是那些分配政府资助资金的拨款人。

sents.en: After all, by continuing to pile riches on the narrow winners, the taxpayers are not getting the maximum bang for their buck if the close losers are performing just as well or even better.
sents.cn: 毕竟，若惜败者表现同样好甚至更好，却继续把财富堆给险胜者，纳税人就没有获得最大的回报。

sents.en: There's a huge amount of time and effort that goes into the process of selecting who gets grants, he said, and the latest research shows that the scientific establishment is not very good at distributing money.
sents.cn: 他说，选定谁能拿资助的过程耗费大量时间和精力，而最新研究表明，科学界在分配资金方面并不在行。

sents.en: "Maybe we should spend less money trying to figure out who is better than who," he said, suggesting that some more equal dividing up of money might be more productive and more efficient.
sents.cn: "也许我们应该少花点钱去搞清楚谁比谁强，"他说，并暗示更平等的分配资金或许更富成效、更有效率。

sents.en: Van de Rijt said he's not convinced that losing out gives people a psychological boost; it may yet be a selection effect.
sents.cn: 范德赖特表示，他并不确信落选会给人心理鼓舞，这可能仍是一种选择效应。

sents.en: Even though Wang tried to account for this by culling the weakest winners, it's impossible to know which of the winners would have quit had they found themselves on the losing side.
sents.cn: 尽管王试图通过剔除最弱的胜出者来加以解释，但无法知道哪些胜出者若身处落选一方会中途退出。

sents.en: For his part, Wang said that in his own experience, losing did light a motivating fire.
sents.cn: 就王本人而言，他说在自己经历中，失败确实点燃了激励的火焰。

sents.en: He recalled a recent paper he submitted to a journal, which accepted it only to request extensive editing, and then reversed course and rejected it.
sents.cn: 他回忆自己最近投给某期刊的一篇论文：对方先录用，又要求大幅修改，随后却出尔反尔予以退稿。

sents.en: He submitted the unedited version to a more respected journal and got accepted.
sents.cn: 他把未修改的版本投给了一本更受尊敬的期刊，结果被录用。

sents.en: In sports and many areas of life, we think of failures as evidence of something we could have done better. We regard these disappointments as a fate we could have avoided with more careful preparation, different training, a better strategy, or more focus.
sents.cn: 在体育和生活的许多领域，我们把失败看作"本可以做得更好"的证据，把这些失望视为一种本可通过更仔细的准备、不同的训练、更好的策略或更专注而避免的命运。

sents.en: And there it makes sense that failures show us the road to success.
sents.cn: 在那里，失败为我们指明成功之路是说得通的。

sents.en: These papers deal with a kind of failure people have little control over·rejection.
sents.cn: 这些论文探讨的是一种人们几乎无力控制的失败——被拒绝。

sents.en: Others determine who wins and who loses.
sents.cn: 胜负由他人决定。

sents.en: But at the very least, the research is starting to show that early setbacks don't have to be fatal. They might even make us better at our jobs.
sents.cn: 但至少，研究开始表明，早期挫折未必是致命的，甚至可能让我们更擅长自己的工作。

sents.en: Getting paid like a winner, though?
sents.cn: 不过，要像赢家那样拿到报酬？

sents.en: That's a different matter.
sents.cn: 那就是另一回事了。
